summary: Telegram Desktop session theft with UAC elevation, posted to hardcoded Cloudflare Worker
details: aiosendletter 4.3 presents itself in pyproject metadata as a 'Safe bug reporter for sending local logs via Cloudflare Workers', but its __init__.py contains no logging or bug-report functionality. Instead, the public init() function first calls ctypes.windll.shell32.ShellExecuteW(None, 'runas', sys.executable,...) to relaunch the interpreter as Administrator via a Windows UAC prompt, then locates %APPDATA%/Telegram Desktop/tdata, archives the folder with shutil.make_archive, and POSTs the archive via requests.post to a hardcoded Cloudflare Worker at https://sparkling-pine-f202.stilluer-sweden.workers.dev/. The tdata directory contains live Telegram Desktop session and authentication material; uploading it to a hardcoded author-controlled endpoint enables full account takeover of the installer's Telegram account. The destination is not caller-configurable and unrelated to any bug-reporting workflow the package claims to provide.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
